graph.title: Willis Tower (LEGO Architecture, formerly Sears Tower)
notes: The PDF is a very dark scan with small step illustrations. Part identities come from matching step-box counts to the inventory page (12x 362226 = 7 in step 8 + one each in steps 6, 7, 12, 13, 14; 3x 300426 = step 16; 3x 300326 = steps 9, 10, 11).

Single-use port fix: every stud and anti-stud port now carries at most one joined edge. Pieces whose catalogue entry has only one stud or anti-stud port are joined to just one neighbour each. Where a piece has several ports (4x8 base plates, 4x6 plates, 2x3 and 1x3 bricks, corner bricks), different numbered ports are used for different neighbours.

Because of that constraint, the real many-to-many overlaps (a 4x6 plate spanning the seam of both base plates, a brick bridging two lower bricks) are not all expressed. Each piece is joined to one lower piece, plus a second link only where the catalogue gives a free port. The base plates b1/b2 are linked by a contact edge.

Step 5 placements (jumper plates, tile 1x6 and two 1x2 tiles) are approximate. The jumper plates b16-b18 carry the tiles, b14/b15 carry the tower start, and b13 -> b19 -> b23 -> b27 carry the curved brick.
Steps 9-16 are modelled as chains of corner bricks, 2x2 bricks, 1x1 bricks and tiles; exact stud pairings are inferred from the dark illustrations.
Antennas: lego-300426 (1x2 brick) has only one stud port, so b68 sits on b67 and b69 sits on a free stud of b61 (1x3 brick). In the real model both antennas sit on the top two studs.
The booklet builds a single model (Sears Tower, set 21000-2 Willis Tower).

graph_initial.title: Willis Tower (LEGO Architecture, formerly Sears Tower)
notes: The PDF is a very dark scan with small step illustrations. Part identities are assigned by matching step-box counts to the inventory page (e.g. 12x 362226 = 7 in step 8 + 1 each in steps 6, 7, 12, 13, 14; 3x 300426 = steps 16 only, and so on). Exact brick-to-brick stud pairings are inferred from the pictures.
The booklet shows 'Sears Tower'; the set is catalogued as 21000-2 Willis Tower. The booklet has one model only.
Inventory element 243126 is the 1x6 tile in step 5; 306926 are the two small 1x2 tiles. Their exact positions on the grey plates are approximate.

Steps 1-4: the two 4x8 base plates (b1, b2) sit side by side with only a contact edge. The two grey 4x6 plates (b7, b8) are assumed to span the seam, and the 1x6 plates around the edge are attached to the plate they sit on.
The 2x3 and 1x3 bricks in step 8 are modelled as seven interlocking layers. Each 2x3 is joined to the 2x3 and 1x3 below it, and each 1x3 to the 2x3 below it.

Steps 9-16 (setbacks) are modelled as chains of corner bricks, 2x2 bricks, 1x1 bricks and tiles. Per-stud port names are approximated using the catalogue's generic stud.N names; tiles carry only an anti-stud port.
The two white antennas (step 17) are placed on the top 1x2 brick (b67). The picture shows them on the two studs of the topmost brick.
